name: acf-whip
description: Hostile workflow enforcer. Zero tolerance backlog automation from decomposition to acceptance with aggressive quality gates. Worktree ownership scoping + configurable namespace (2.4.0, from a field report that /go's startup pruned unrelated worktrees): acf-whip now manages ONLY worktrees on its own branch namespace (<ACFW_BRANCH_PREFIX>/<slug>, default worktree/<slug>). The doctor's orphan reaper and wrong-branch FATAL — which the /go bootstrap runs with --fix on every start — skip any directory under the worktree dir that is on a foreign branch, detached (mid-rebase), or not a registered worktree, so a research/benchmark worktree you keep in the same repo (even parked under .worktree/) is never force-removed. The worktree directory and branch prefix are configurable via .backlog/.acfw-config (ACFW_WORKTREE_DIR default .worktree, ACFW_BRANCH_PREFIX default worktree), threaded through clean-checkout/integrate/doctor/scan and emitted in the scan digest so /go prompts reference the configured prefix; defaults preserve prior behavior exactly. Worktrees-live-at-repo-root/.worktree/ (gitignored, ephemeral) is now a documented ACF organization convention. Regression-tested by tests/phase1-doctor-hydrate (foreign-worktree-survives + custom-namespace round-trip). Orchestrator hardening (2.3.0, from a field bug report): (1) the /go workflow now STREAMS each dispatched unit through its own review+integration lifecycle instead of holding the whole wave at a per-iteration barrier — a fast task is reviewed, accepted, and integrated while a multi-hour task in the same wave is still running (the single-writer and topological-integration invariants are preserved by explicit serialization, not the barrier; behaviorally tested in tests/phase5-streaming). (2) A read-only scan that fails to emit StructuredOutput no longer ABORTS the run: it falls back to a schema-less text scan (parse the JSON the model printed), and if even that fails it degrades to a graceful 'scan-degraded' stop + drain off the last good snapshot instead of discarding hours of healthy iterations (tests/phase4-scan-degrade). (3) New /whip-move operator command wraps the apply-transition.sh writer so manual last-mile close-out (move a task, set Integrated-At, add a dependency) is a validated one-liner instead of raw perl/sed (tests/phase4-whip-move). (4) A specialist may report blocked_reason=dependency-missing + needs_task; the orchestrator then parks the task for an operator immediately (naming the task to create) instead of re-dispatching it until the Block-Count cap. (5) Per-wave dispatch logging names what is in flight. Per-ticket latency optimization (2.2.0): the /go workflow's per-iteration scan now uses scan-backlog.sh --digest (a small scheduling snapshot — counts + actionable tasks + accepted integration candidates + a compact satisfiedDeps list, with terminal-accepted tasks collapsed and the accepted folder classified in one batched grep+awk pass) and whip-doctor --active-only (full integrity over active folders, accepted fed as cheap batched stubs), cutting a lived-in backlog's per-iteration scan+recheck from tens of seconds to ~2s and shrinking the verbatim scan echo from ~50KB to <1KB; the deterministic shell-runner agents (scan, single writer, integrate, bootstrap, drain) run on a fast model (overridable via the shellModel arg) while specialists/reviewers/conflict-resolvers keep the session model. Digest correctness is unit-tested (tests/phase2-scheduler satisfiedDeps cases) and the active-only doctor parity is regression-tested (tests/phase1-doctor-hydrate). /task and /go run as dynamic workflows (deterministic loop, schema-enforced worktree slugs, integrity-gated) when available, with the legacy single-context loop as automatic fallback. The /go workflow performs the FULL state machine — including blocked→pending unblock when dependencies resolve and in-progress→blocked timeout at the operator threshold (ACFW_INPROGRESS_TIMEOUT_HOURS, default 8h) — so a backlog with pending tasks gated on blocked tasks runs to completion instead of stalling (2.0.3). Self-heals pre-2.0.0 backlogs: the doctor derives missing worktree slugs for active tasks and treats accepted/historical tasks as advisory (never blocking); /go counts branchless historical accepted tasks as terminal. /task aborts up front when no specialist agents are installed (rather than emitting a backlog /go's gate would reject). Planning and execution default to maximum parallelism of non-conflicting work. Scales to large lived-in backlogs: the scheduler runs on a bounded working-set snapshot (terminal/historical accepted collapse into aggregate counts; retained dependency targets are emitted slim), so the per-iteration scan stays small instead of stalling the workflow agent. Reliability hardening (2.1.0): every schema agent() call is wrapped in bounded retry + graceful degrade, so a single StructuredOutput non-emit no longer aborts a multi-hour run; a durable per-task Block-Count breaks the specialist re-dispatch livelock (a task whose real blocker is unmodeled stops being re-queued after a cap and is surfaced as needsOperator instead of spinning); apply-transition syncs the Status frontmatter to the destination folder atomically with the move (a stale Status no longer self-inflicts a doctor FATAL that aborted /go at its first transition — the doctor now treats status-folder-mismatch as REPAIRABLE); completion requires no pending unblock so a dependency integrated in the final iteration never strands its blocked dependent; integrate-worktree treats an empty (no-commits-ahead) branch as terminal so a read-only/gate task never hangs the count; and transition rows splice into the Transition Log table and cap, keeping task files well-formed and bounded. Scheduling/terminal logic is unit-tested (tests/phase2-scheduler); the shell layer is regression-tested (tests/phase3-reliability).
